title: Reading Drill — Studying wait times at a clinic — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Studying wait times at a clinic — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Ravensmere, work on patients seeing late arrivals called first had already produced a small collection of anonymous arrival records. The clinic administrator used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: time from check-in to being called.

**B** The group kept a display explaining the appointment order for the new trial, which was planned to run for seven weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that urgent cases should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
